entities.text: High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By way of the present petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner has assailed the order dated 25.03.2022 passed by the learned ADM (West), Appellate Authority in Appeal No.1/2022 titled as Rajinder Kumar Bharti v. Tata Power Delhi Distribution Ltd.

entities.text: Rajinder Kumar Bharti v. Tata Power Delhi Distribution Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner also seeks directions to the respondent to not take any coercive action against him.
2. Vide the impugned order, the petitioner was directed to pre-deposit 50% of the assessment amount in terms of Section 127(2) of the Indian Electricity Act, 2003.

3. During the course of submissions, the petitioner has referred to a notice dated 13.02.2019 issued on behalf of the respondent, asking him to provide a valid Factory License, failing which he was to be considered as Non-Domestic category consumer for the purposes of billing of electricity consumption.

He submits that in the said notice, it was mentioned that 'Industrial' Power tariff shall be applicable only to consumers who held valid Factory License, and an FSSAI (Food Safety and Standards Authority of India) license could be considered as valid Factory License as per DERC orders.

entities.text: FSSAI (Food Safety and Standards Authority of India)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is the grievance of the petitioner that in pursuance of the notice, an FSSAI license issued on 22.02.2021 was submitted to the respondent, yet his case was not covered under the 'Industrial'
category.

4. The petitioner has also contended that the aforesaid assessment amount was not mentioned in the final assessment order issued on 07.02.2022 and further, that no break-up of the same was ever Rajinder Kumar Bharti vs Tata Power Delhi Distribution Limited on 20 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62345989/
1 provided to him.

entities.text: Rajinder Kumar Bharti vs Tata Power Delhi Distribution Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Mr. Akhil Hasija, learned counsel for the respondent, on the other hand, has submitted that the petitioner is engaged in the business of Food Services - Food Vending Establishment, Digitally Signed 13:20:58 which stands covered not under the 'Industrial' but the 'Commercial' category.
As such, he has defended the final assessment order.

6. Insofar as the second contention raised on behalf of the petitioner is concerned, learned counsel for the respondent has referred to the impugned order, wherein it is noted that alongwith the provisional order a calculation sheet was handed over to the petitioner, vide which the assessed amount of Rs.16,61,717/70/- was intimated.
He submits that the petitioner has not denied the receipt of the aforesaid calculation sheet at any point of time.

In support of his submissions, learned counsel has also referred to the order dated 08.11.2019 passed by a Co- ordinate Bench of this Court in Kolmet Enterprises and Another v. New Delhi Municipal Council reported as 2019 SCC OnLine Del 11061.
7.

entities.text: Kolmet Enterprises and Another v. New Delhi Municipal Council reported as 2019 SCC OnLine Del 11061
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this stage, the petitioner submits that he is ready and willing to make pre-deposit of 50% of the assessment amount, however, in view of the financial constraints suffered by him, sufficient time may be granted to do the same.

8. Keeping in view the above submissions, this Court deems it apposite to direct that the pre-deposit of 50% of the assessment amount be made by the petitioner before the Appellate Authority within 8 weeks from today.
9. With the above directions, the present petition is disposed of, alongwith the pending application.
10. Needless to state that while passing the present order, this Court has not gone into the merits of the submissions made by the parties.
As such, it shall be open to both the parties to raise their respective contentions before the concerned Appellate Authority, as available to them in accordance with law.
MANOJ KUMAR OHRI, J APRIL 20, 2022 na
